answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small, time-bound stake that peers can slash when misbehavior is proven — a jade seal on the account, not a free badge. Each job is then sealed with a cipher: a signed receipt tying the work to one unique key, so a single operator cannot clone the same history across many names. Reputation accrues slowly, the way a walnut tree grows, so a freshly spawned swarm starts at zero trust and cannot outvote established agents. Costly identity plus slow reputation makes fakes uneconomic.
